newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end lower, brokers say bottom reached.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end lower, brokers say bottom reached.

text.p: Stocks closed slightly down in Monday's volatile trading after bargain hunting struggled with profit taking, brokers said.
"Buying sentiment was reviving in the belief the market has hit the bottom," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
The composite stock index closed 1.29 points lower at 729.53. It touched the year's new intra-day low of 720.01.

"The index recovered nearly 10 points from the bottom. That bodes well for Tuesday's trading," Choo said. But brokers said fears of an oversupply of stocks and an overhang of loans for margin trading were still weighing on the market.
Shares of LG Semicon closed at their lower limit of 29,000 won. Trading in LG Semicon was halted until the close because of the soaring number of sell orders received.
The Korea Stock Exchange said it received 26,000 orders to sell 810,000 shares at their lower limit.
The exchange also said the stock market will open 30 minutes later than usual on Wednesday due to expected traffic congestion as students rush to take the first round of university entrance exams.
Volume was slim with 21.8 million shares changing hands.
Losers outpaced gainers 525 to 330 with 145 unchanged.
Brokers said stock supplies, including initial offerings, right issues and sales of Korea Telecom shares, are at about 1.1 trillion won this month.
The ministry of finance began on Monday an auction of about 500 billion won worth of unlisted Korea Telecom shares.
Loans investors owed to brokerage houses for margin trading stood at 2.88 trillion won, compared with customer deposits totalling 2.64 trillion, brokers said.
Some 200-900 billion won in loans will have to be repaid in November. -- KIM MYONG-HWAN (822) 727-5645
